title: Chapter 10 — Uncle Dozie Comes to Lagos
description: Uncle Dozie arrives with a sack of garri and a scheme. He also knows something about Papa's debts.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Two weeks after the burial. 6 a.m. Someone is banging on the shop shutter with a shoe.

beats.speaker: uncleDozie
beats.text: Nephew! (He has a sack of garri, a radio and no plan to leave.) Lagos! Finally! Your father always said I would make it here one day.

beats.speaker: uncleDozie
beats.text: You remember the land business. My twenty per cent was... modest. Lagos owes me the rest.

variants.text: Your mother refused to sell the land. Stubborn woman. So now I am here to find my own fortune. With your help, of course.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: By Wednesday Dozie has a business card. DOZIE & ASSOCIATES: LAND, LANDED PROPERTY AND LAND MATTERS.

beats.speaker: uncleDozie
beats.text: Your Mama Ngozi. Twenty-two years of savings in that stall. She wants land in Lekki for her old age. I have a plot. (He doesn't have a plot.) You are the honest-faced one. You will introduce me.

beats.speaker: uncleDozie
beats.text: Forty thousand for you. Just for your face.

options.text: Go straight to Ngozi and warn her about your own uncle.

beats.speaker: ngozi
beats.text: (She looks at Dozie's business card for a long time, then tears it into exactly eight pieces.) You warned me about your own blood. (She nods once.) I will remember this, Emeka.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Three days later, Ngozi's nephew, who is a policeman, comes looking for "Dozie and Associates".

escaped.toast: You lose them behind the motor park. Dozie is already on a bus to Onitsha. With most of the money.

caught.toast: ₦20,000 to settle it at the station. Ngozi doesn't look at you any more.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Dozie's last night. He drinks two bottles of Ike's Hennessy and becomes a different, sadder uncle.

beats.speaker: uncleDozie
beats.text: Your father's debts. You think it was school fees? (He laughs.) It was a loan from a man in Onitsha. A man who wore white. He lent Papa money and asked for "something small" in return. Papa said no.

beats.speaker: uncleDozie
beats.text: They never collected the money, Emeka. They didn't want the money. They wanted the no to become a yes. Your father died saying no.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Your phone is in your pocket. He is drunk. He will never say this again.

beats.speaker: uncleDozie
beats.text: (He is crying now, into the garri sack.) Send me home, nephew. Or let me stay. Lagos is too big for a small thief like me.

options.text: Pay his bus fare home. "Go and tell Nne the truth about Papa. All of it."
"Stay, Uncle. There's space on the floor."

beats.title: Uncle Dozie Comes to Lagos
beats.summary: Dozie came with a sack of garri and a scheme, and left you a truth: Papa's debts were to men in white, and Papa died saying no.
